metadata.title: Effective closed subshifts in 1D can be implemented in 2D
metadata.authors: Bruno Durand, Andrei Romashchenko, Alexander Shen

nodes.name: Alphabet and letters
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be a finite set called an \emph{alphabet}; its elements are called \emph{letters}.

nodes.name: $A$-configuration
nodes.statement: An $A$-configuration is a mapping $C\colon \mathbb{Z}^2\to A$; cell $(i,j)$ contains letter $C(i,j)$.

nodes.name: Local rule
nodes.statement: A \emph{local rule} is given by a positive integer $M$ and a list of prohibited $M\times M$ patterns; a configuration $C$ \emph{satisfies} $R$ if no listed pattern appears in $C$.

nodes.name: Subset $L(A,B,R,\pi)$
nodes.statement: Given alphabets $A,B$, a local rule $R$ on $A$ forcing vertically constant $\pi$-images, and $\pi\colon A\to B$, $L(A,B,R,\pi)\subset B^{\mathbb{Z}}$ is the set of $\pi$-images of $A$-configurations satisfying $R$.

nodes.name: Interval (base open set)
nodes.statement: In the product topology on $B^{\mathbb{Z}}$, an \emph{interval} is the set of sequences obtained by fixing letters in finitely many positions.

nodes.name: Effectively open / effectively closed set
nodes.statement: An \emph{effectively open} subset of $B^{\mathbb{Z}}$ is a union of a computably enumerable family of intervals; an \emph{effectively closed} set is the complement of an effectively open one.

nodes.name: Subshift
nodes.statement: A \emph{subshift} is a closed subset of $B^{\mathbb{Z}}$ invariant under left and right shifts; an effectively closed subshift is additionally an effectively closed set.

nodes.name: Responsibility zone and delegated bit
nodes.statement: The \emph{responsibility zone} of a macro-tile is the set of bits of the input sequence whose vertical lines cross it; one such bit may be \emph{delegated} to the macro-tile, which then is \emph{responsible} for it.

nodes.name: Extended responsibility zone
nodes.statement: The \emph{extended responsibility zone} of a macro-tile is three times wider than its responsibility zone, covering the macro-tile together with its left and right neighbors (width $3L_k$ for level $k$).

nodes.name: Main theorem: 2D implementation of 1D effectively closed subshifts
nodes.statement: $L(A,B,R,\pi)$ is an effectively closed subshift; conversely, for every effectively closed subshift $S\subset B^{\mathbb{Z}}$ one can find $A$, $R$, $\pi$ with $S = L(A,B,R,\pi)$.
assumptions: $\pi\colon A\to B$ a map forcing vertically aligned $B$-images
$S\subset B^{\mathbb{Z}}$ an effectively closed subshift (for the converse)
conclusions: Every effectively closed subshift is some $L(A,B,R,\pi)$

nodes.name: Berger's aperiodic tile-set theorem
nodes.statement: There exists a finite tile set / local rule whose tilings of the plane are all aperiodic.

nodes.name: Proof of main theorem (forward direction: $L(A,B,R,\pi)$ is effectively closed)
nodes.statement: $L(A,B,R,\pi)$ is shift-invariant; as the continuous image of the compact set of $A$-configurations satisfying $R$ it is compact, and the enumeration of bad $B$-strings effectivizes this argument.

nodes.name: Proof sketch of main theorem (converse direction via fixed-point tilings)
nodes.statement: Modify the fixed-point self-similar tiling of \cite{firstpart} by variable zoom factors, conscious/sub-conscious bit delegation across levels, bit-group checking against an enumeration of forbidden patterns, and extended responsibility zones to handle the degenerate case.

nodes.name: Variable zoom factor
nodes.section: 2 The idea of the construction; 3 Variable zoom factor
nodes.statement: Replace the constant zoom factor by an increasing sequence $N_0,N_1,N_2,\ldots$, so that level-$k$ macro-tiles are $N_{k-1}\times N_{k-1}$ blocks of level-$(k-1)$ macro-tiles, hosting computations of unbounded size; consistency of level information is enforced by side-color matching and per-bit checks among brothers.

nodes.name: Conscious bits and delegation across levels
nodes.statement: Each macro-tile of level $k$ has a responsibility zone of $L_k$ bits and is delegated at most one of them according to its vertical position in the father; consistency between father and son delegations propagates correct bit values from the ground level upward.

nodes.name: Checking bit groups against forbidden patterns
nodes.statement: Each level-$k$ macro-tile checks a bit group of length $l_k$ from its zone against $l_k$ enumeration steps of forbidden patterns; sons make the group available to the computation zone and verify consistency with delegated bits and with the father.

nodes.name: Degenerate case: extended responsibility zone
nodes.statement: To catch substrings straddling the dividing line not crossed by any macro-tile, each macro-tile checks bit groups in its extended responsibility zone (its own zone plus those of its left and right neighbors); cross-boundary brothers compare information about the bit groups of their fathers and uncles.

nodes.name: Final adjustments to parameters
nodes.statement: Choose $N_k = 2^{C 2^k}$ and $l_k = k$ (or similar) so that $\log N_{k+2}\ll N_k$, $N_k\gg L_k$, $l_{k+1}\ll N_{k-1}$, and the enumeration runs for $l_k$ steps fit in the computational zone; all constraints are simultaneously satisfiable.

nodes.name: Generalization to higher dimensions and Cantor alphabets
nodes.statement: The same construction implements $k$-dimensional effectively closed subshifts via $(k+1)$-dimensional SFTs; same-dimension implementation and Cantor-alphabet variants (Hochman's question) are answered negatively, as noted by E.~Jeandel and corollaries of \cite{dls},\cite{rumush}.

nodes.name: Same-dimension implementation / Cantor-alphabet representation
nodes.statement: Can every $k$-dimensional effectively closed subshift be implemented by a tiling of the same dimension $k$? Can every such subshift over a Cantor alphabet be represented as a continuous image of $(k+1)$-dimensional SFT tilings?
